hypotheses.H1_primary: C_final beats C_initial (the best program the generator wrote from scratch inside arm C) on the AUDIT mean score: paired bootstrap Bonferroni-corrected CI of the difference has lower bound > 0, AND C_final differs structurally from C_initial (graph/function-set change or AST similarity < 0.6).
hypotheses.H2: C_final beats B_best (independent sampling, equal budget) on AUDIT (same test).
hypotheses.H3: C_final beats A (one-shot) on AUDIT (same test).
hypotheses.H4: C_final beats H (hand-written baseline) on AUDIT (same test).
hypotheses.H5: C_final beats D (direct Claude call per instance) on AUDIT (same test).
hypotheses.novelty_metric: new algorithm = executable candidate whose AST similarity to every earlier candidate of the same arm is < 0.6; structural mutation per novelty.classify_change; significant improvement = child beats parent on SELECTION with paired bootstrap 95% CI > 0.
hypotheses.statistics: per replicate: mean score with bootstrap 95% CI; 5 paired comparisons, Bonferroni => 99% paired bootstrap CIs over audit instances. Replicates are independent repetitions of the whole search (generator stochasticity); a hypothesis is called SUPPORTED only if it holds in every replicate, MIXED if in some, NOT SUPPORTED if in none.
hypotheses.leakage_controls: generator sees: public spec, format examples, parent programs, and for DEV instances the input, its own output, score and the checker's violation text (no reference, no bound). SELECTION: aggregate scores only, used for parent/champion choice. AUDIT: never used before the final single evaluation.
hypotheses.success_criterion: Stage succeeds iff H1_primary holds. Otherwise the result is reported as negative.
